b1-01.title: Offices and documents: codice fiscale, residence, permit

steps.title: Saying what you need
steps.how_to: How to say what you need and what you have to do at an office.
steps.intro: At an Italian office you'll hear bisogna for what you have to do and serve or servono for what you need. You can use them yourself to ask what to bring.

examples.said: Bisogna prendere il numero.
examples.en: You have to take a ticket.

examples.said: Serve una marca da bollo da sedici euro.
examples.en: You need a sixteen-euro revenue stamp.

examples.said: Servono due fototessere.
examples.en: You need two passport photos.

examples.said: Bisogna prendere l'appuntamento online?
examples.en: Do you have to book the appointment online?

steps.notice: Bisogna is followed by a verb and never changes; serve and servono are followed by the thing you need, servono for more than one, because the thing is what's needed.
steps.context: Italian offices often want an appointment booked online and a marca da bollo bought beforehand at a tabaccheria.

ask.said: Sei all'anagrafe e c'è la fila. Cosa fai prima?
ask.en: You're at the registry office and there's a line. What do you do first?

answer.said: Prima bisogna prendere il numero.
answer.en: First you have to take a ticket.

ask.said: Cosa porti in comune per la residenza?
ask.en: What do you bring to city hall to register your residence?

answer.said: Servono il passaporto e il contratto d'affitto.
answer.en: You need your passport and your lease.

ask.said: Per il permesso di soggiorno, cosa porti in questura?
ask.en: For your residence permit, what do you bring to the questura?

answer.said: Servono la ricevuta e quattro fototessere.
answer.en: You need the receipt and four passport photos.

mission.goal: Ask what you need to register your residence.

say.said: Buongiorno, devo richiedere la residenza. Cosa serve?
say.en: Good morning, I need to register my residence. What do I need?

steps.title: Checking what's enough
steps.how_to: How to ask whether something is enough with basta.
steps.intro: Basta means that something is enough, or that all you have to do is one thing. It's how you check with a clerk whether a copy will do.

examples.said: Per il contratto basta la fotocopia?
examples.en: For the lease, is a photocopy enough?

examples.said: Sì, basta la fotocopia.
examples.en: Yes, a photocopy is enough.

examples.said: Basta firmare qui.
examples.en: You just need to sign here.

examples.said: Bastano due righe.
examples.en: Two lines are enough.

steps.notice: Basta plus a thing means that thing is enough, and basta plus a verb means that's all you have to do; with more than one thing it's bastano, because it matches what's enough.
steps.context: Italian offices usually ask for the original and a photocopy of every document.

ask.said: Hai solo la fotocopia del contratto. Cosa chiedi all'impiegata?
ask.en: You only have a photocopy of your lease. What do you ask the clerk?

answer.said: Basta la fotocopia?
answer.en: Is a photocopy enough?

ask.said: Hai perso l'autocertificazione. Cosa devi fare?
ask.en: You lost your self-certification form. What do you have to do?

answer.said: Basta compilare di nuovo il modulo.
answer.en: I just have to fill out the form again.

ask.said: Il tuo amico vuole portare dieci fototessere. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: Your friend wants to bring ten passport photos. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Bastano quattro fototessere.
answer.en: Four passport photos are enough.

mission.goal: Ask whether a photocopy of your lease is enough.

say.said: Per il contratto basta la fotocopia?
say.en: For the lease, is a photocopy enough?

steps.title: Asking how long it takes
steps.how_to: How to ask and say how long something takes with ci vuole and ci vogliono.
steps.intro: Ci vuole and ci vogliono say how long something takes. You'll use them to ask about any application or permit.

examples.said: Quanto tempo ci vuole?
examples.en: How long does it take?

examples.said: Ci vuole un mese.
examples.en: It takes a month.

examples.said: Ci vogliono alcune settimane.
examples.en: It takes a few weeks.

examples.said: E quanto tempo ci vuole per avere il permesso nuovo?
examples.en: And how long does it take to get the new permit?

steps.notice: Ci vuole goes with one thing or amount and ci vogliono with more than one, because it agrees with the time it takes.

ask.said: Vuoi sapere quando è pronta la tua pratica. Cosa chiedi?
ask.en: You want to know when your application will be ready. What do you ask?

answer.said: Quanto tempo ci vuole?
answer.en: How long does it take?

ask.said: Il permesso nuovo è pronto domani?
ask.en: Is the new permit ready tomorrow?

answer.said: No, ci vogliono alcune settimane.
answer.en: No, it takes a few weeks.

ask.said: Per la residenza, quanto aspetti di solito?
ask.en: For residence registration, how long do you usually wait?

answer.said: Di solito ci vogliono quarantacinque giorni.
answer.en: It usually takes forty-five days.

mission.goal: Ask how long your application will take.

say.said: Quanto tempo ci vuole?
say.en: How long does it take?

steps.title: Following a clerk's instructions
steps.how_to: How to understand the polite instructions a clerk gives you.
steps.intro: Clerks give instructions with the polite command form. Once you know the endings, you can follow them without asking for English.

examples.said: Compili il modulo.
examples.en: Fill out the form.

examples.said: Firmi qui in fondo.
examples.en: Sign here at the bottom.

examples.said: Prenda il numero e aspetti.
examples.en: Take a ticket and wait.

examples.said: Torni con la ricevuta fra trenta giorni.
examples.en: Come back with the receipt in thirty days.

steps.notice: A polite instruction ends in -i for -are verbs and in -a for -ere and -ire verbs, so firmi means "sign," not "you sign."

ask.said: Cosa ti dice l'impiegata quando ti dà il modulo?
ask.en: What does the clerk tell you when she hands you the form?

answer.said: Compili il modulo e firmi qui in fondo.
answer.en: Fill out the form and sign here at the bottom.

ask.said: All'anagrafe c'è la fila. Cosa ti dice l'impiegato?
ask.en: There's a line at the registry office. What does the clerk tell you?

answer.said: Prenda il numero e aspetti.
answer.en: Take a ticket and wait.

ask.said: La tua pratica non è finita. Cosa ti dice l'impiegato?
ask.en: Your application isn't done yet. What does the clerk tell you?

answer.said: Torni con la ricevuta fra trenta giorni.
answer.en: Come back with the receipt in thirty days.

mission.goal: Ask the clerk what to do next and follow the instructions.

say.said: Mi scusi, cosa devo fare adesso?
say.en: Excuse me, what do I do now?

steps.title: Asking which and how come
steps.how_to: How to ask which one, how come and how far along.
steps.intro: Quale, come mai and a che punto let you ask exactly what you need at an office. You'll use them at the counter and on the phone.

examples.said: Quale modulo devo compilare?
examples.en: Which form do I need to fill out?

examples.said: Quali documenti servono?
examples.en: Which documents do I need?

examples.said: Buongiorno, chiamo per sapere a che punto è la mia pratica.
examples.en: Good morning, I'm calling to find out where my application stands.

examples.said: Come mai ci vuole così tanto?
examples.en: How come it's taking so long?

steps.notice: Quale picks one from a set and quali more than one, because it agrees; come mai asks "how come," and a che punto asks how far along something is.

ask.said: Ci sono tre moduli sul tavolo. Cosa chiedi?
ask.en: There are three forms on the table. What do you ask?

answer.said: Quale modulo devo compilare?
answer.en: Which form do I need to fill out?

ask.said: Aspetti la tua pratica da due mesi. Cosa chiedi al telefono?
ask.en: You've been waiting on your application for two months. What do you ask on the phone?

answer.said: Buongiorno, a che punto è la mia pratica?
answer.en: Good morning, where does my application stand?

ask.said: Al telefono ti dicono che manca un documento. Come rispondi?
ask.en: On the phone they tell you a document is missing. How do you answer?

answer.said: Come mai? L'ho consegnato a maggio!
answer.en: How come? I turned it in in May!

mission.goal: Ask how far along your application is.

say.said: Buongiorno, a che punto è la mia pratica?
say.en: Good morning, where does my application stand?

b1-02.title: Doing things for people: combined pronouns

steps.title: Bringing it to you
steps.how_to: How to say "it to me" and "it to you" with me lo, te la and the rest.
steps.intro: Two small words together, like me lo or te la, say "it to me" or "it to you." You'll use them to offer, lend and ask for things without naming them again.

examples.said: Me lo incarta, per favore? È un regalo.
examples.en: Could you wrap it for me, please? It's a gift.

examples.said: Sì, scusa! Te la porto subito.
examples.en: Yes, sorry! I'll bring it right over.

examples.said: Se ti serve il trapano, te lo presto volentieri.
examples.en: If you need the drill, I'm happy to lend it to you.

examples.said: Le chiavi? Te le restituisco stasera.
examples.en: The keys? I'll give them back to you tonight.

steps.notice: The "to whom" word comes first and mi or ti become me or te, then lo, la, li or le for the thing, because it matches the thing: la for the ladder, le for the keys.
steps.context: In almost any shop you can say "È un regalo" and they'll gift-wrap it for free.

ask.said: Un amico ti chiede i tuoi libri. Cosa rispondi?
ask.en: A friend asks to borrow your books. What do you say?

answer.said: Te li presto volentieri.
answer.en: I'm happy to lend them to you.

ask.said: La tua vicina vuole indietro la sua scala. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: Your neighbor wants her ladder back. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Te la porto subito.
answer.en: I'll bring it right over.

ask.said: Compri un libro per un'amica. Cosa chiedi al libraio?
ask.en: You're buying a book for a friend. What do you ask the bookseller?

answer.said: Me lo incarta, per favore? È un regalo.
answer.en: Could you wrap it for me, please? It's a gift.

mission.goal: Ask the shopkeeper to gift-wrap what you bought.

say.said: Me lo incarta, per favore? È un regalo.
say.en: Could you wrap it for me, please? It's a gift.

steps.title: Doing it for someone else
steps.how_to: How to say "it to him," "it to her" or "it to you" with glielo.
steps.intro: Glielo says "it to him," "it to her," or "it to you" when you're being polite. You'll hear it in every shop and use it to pass things on.

examples.said: Glielo dico io.
examples.en: I'll tell him.

examples.said: Gliela incarto subito.
examples.en: I'll wrap it for you right away.

examples.said: Glielo taglio sottile come prima?
examples.en: Should I slice it thin for you, like before?

examples.said: Sì, glielo scrivo qui.
examples.en: Sure, I'll write it down for you here.

steps.notice: Gli, le and Le all become glie- and join lo, la, li or le as one word, so the same glielo means to him, to her or to you; the situation tells you who.

ask.said: Il libraio ti chiede il numero di telefono. Cosa rispondi?
ask.en: The bookseller asks for your phone number. What do you say?

answer.said: Sì, glielo scrivo qui.
answer.en: Sure, I'll write it down for you here.

ask.said: Marco non sa niente della festa. Cosa dici agli amici?
ask.en: Marco doesn't know anything about the party. What do you tell your friends?

answer.said: Glielo dico io.
answer.en: I'll tell him.

ask.said: Lavori in un negozio e una signora compra un regalo. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: You work in a shop and a woman buys a gift. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Glielo incarto subito.
answer.en: I'll wrap it for you right away.

mission.goal: Offer to pass a message on to someone.

say.said: Non ti preoccupare, glielo dico io.
say.en: Don't worry, I'll tell him.

steps.title: Asking for a bit more
steps.how_to: How to ask for some more of something with me ne.
steps.intro: Me ne dà means "could you give me some" or "could you give me two." It's what you say at the deli counter when you want more.

examples.said: È buonissimo. Me ne dà ancora un etto?
examples.en: It's delicious. Could I have another hundred grams?

examples.said: Me ne dà un pezzetto da assaggiare?
examples.en: Could I have a little piece to taste?

examples.said: Me ne dà due, per favore.
examples.en: Could I have two, please?

examples.said: Te ne porto due.
examples.en: I'll bring you two.

steps.notice: Ne means "of it" or "of them" and joins like lo, so mi becomes me: me ne dà due; with an amount, ne is always there, because the amount is of something.

ask.said: Il prosciutto è buonissimo. Cosa chiedi al salumiere?
ask.en: The prosciutto is delicious. What do you ask the deli man?

answer.said: Me ne dà ancora un etto?
answer.en: Could I have another hundred grams?

ask.said: Vuoi assaggiare il pecorino. Cosa chiedi?
ask.en: You want to taste the pecorino. What do you ask?

answer.said: Me ne dà un pezzetto da assaggiare?
answer.en: Could I have a little piece to taste?

ask.said: Un amico non ha bicchieri per la festa. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A friend doesn't have glasses for the party. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Te ne porto due.
answer.en: I'll bring you two.

mission.goal: Ask for another hundred grams at the deli counter.

say.said: Me ne dà ancora un etto?
say.en: Could I have another hundred grams?

steps.title: Saying who gave what
steps.how_to: How to say "I gave it to you" in the past, with the right ending.
steps.intro: In the past, me lo and glielo go before ho or hai, as in te l'ho data. You'll use it to say who gave, lent or sent what.

examples.said: Le chiavi della cantina? Te le ho date io, no?
examples.en: The basement keys? I gave them to you, didn't I?

examples.said: Quel libro? Gliel'ho già ordinato.
examples.en: That book? I already ordered it for you.

examples.said: Te l'ho data ieri, la chiave.
examples.en: I gave you the key yesterday.

examples.said: Me li hai prestati tu.
examples.en: You're the one who lent them to me.

steps.notice: Lo and la shorten to l' before ho, and the ending matches the thing, data for la chiave and date for le chiavi, because it follows what was given, not the person.

ask.said: Un amico sa già la notizia. Cosa gli chiedi?
ask.en: A friend already knows the news. What do you ask him?

answer.said: Chi te l'ha detto?
answer.en: Who told you?

ask.said: Dov'è la chiave del tuo vicino?
ask.en: Where's your neighbor's key?

answer.said: Gliel'ho data ieri.
answer.en: I gave it to him yesterday.

ask.said: Hai ancora i libri della tua vicina?
ask.en: Do you still have your neighbor's books?

answer.said: No, glieli ho già restituiti.
answer.en: No, I already gave them back to her.

mission.goal: Tell your neighbor you already gave back the keys.

say.said: Te le ho già restituite ieri.
say.en: I already gave them back to you yesterday.

steps.title: Offering to do it
steps.how_to: How to use me lo or glielo with posso, può and an infinitive.
steps.intro: With posso or può, the pair goes before the verb or at the end of the infinitive, as in posso portartelo. You'll use it to offer help and to ask for it.

examples.said: Posso ordinarglielo. Arriva in due giorni.
examples.en: I can order it for you. It'll be here in two days.

examples.said: Posso portartelo stasera, se vuoi.
examples.en: I can bring it over tonight if you want.

examples.said: Me lo può spiegare?
examples.en: Could you explain it to me?

examples.said: Te lo posso portare domani.
examples.en: I can bring it to you tomorrow.

steps.notice: The pair goes before posso or può, or joins the end of the infinitive as one word, which drops its last e: portartelo; the two pronouns always stay together.

ask.said: Non capisci il modulo. Cosa chiedi all'impiegata?
ask.en: You don't understand the form. What do you ask the clerk?

answer.said: Me lo può spiegare, per favore?
answer.en: Could you explain it to me, please?

ask.said: Un'amica ha bisogno del tuo caricabatterie stasera. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: A friend needs your charger tonight. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Posso portartelo stasera, se vuoi.
answer.en: I can bring it over tonight if you want.

ask.said: Un cliente cerca un libro, ma in negozio non c'è. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A customer is looking for a book, but it's not in the store. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Posso ordinarglielo, se vuole.
answer.en: I can order it for you, if you'd like.

mission.goal: Offer to bring something over to a friend.

say.said: Posso portartelo stasera, se vuoi.
say.en: I can bring it over tonight if you want.

steps.title: Forgetting and remembering it
steps.how_to: How to say "I forgot about it" with me ne.
steps.intro: Verbs like dimenticarsi and ricordarsi take ne for "about it," as in me ne sono dimenticato. You'll use it to apologize and to check on things.

examples.said: Me ne sono dimenticato!
examples.en: I forgot all about it!

examples.said: Scusa, me ne sono dimenticata!
examples.en: Sorry, I forgot all about it!

examples.said: Te ne sei ricordata?
examples.en: Did you remember?

examples.said: Se n'è andato presto.
examples.en: He left early.

steps.notice: Ne stands for "about it," so me ne, te ne and se ne come before the verb even where English has nothing; a woman says dimenticata.

ask.said: Non hai portato la scala alla vicina. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: You didn't bring the ladder back to your neighbor. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Scusa, me ne sono dimenticato!
answer.en: Sorry, I forgot all about it!

ask.said: Un'amica doveva portare le chiavi. Cosa le chiedi?
ask.en: A friend was supposed to bring the keys. What do you ask her?

answer.said: Te ne sei ricordata?
answer.en: Did you remember?

ask.said: Il tuo amico non è più alla festa. Cosa è successo?
ask.en: Your friend isn't at the party anymore. What happened?

answer.said: Se n'è andato presto.
answer.en: He left early.

mission.goal: Apologize to your neighbor for forgetting something.

say.said: Scusa, me ne sono dimenticato!
say.en: Sorry, I forgot all about it!

steps.title: Describing things with che
steps.how_to: How to describe a person or thing with che.
steps.intro: Che joins two ideas, as in "the bank my landlady recommended." You'll use it to say exactly which account, card or person you mean.

examples.said: È la banca che mi ha consigliato la padrona di casa.
examples.en: It's the bank my landlady recommended.

examples.said: L'impiegata che mi ha aiutato è molto gentile.
examples.en: The clerk who helped me is really nice.

examples.said: Il conto che ho aperto è gratuito.
examples.en: The account I opened is free.

examples.said: Sì, è quella che mi avete dato la settimana scorsa.
examples.en: Yes, it's the one you gave me last week.

steps.notice: Che links a person or thing to what you say about it, whether it does the action or receives it; Italian always says che, even where English drops "that."

ask.said: Chi ti ha consigliato questa banca?
ask.en: Who recommended this bank to you?

answer.said: È la banca che mi ha consigliato la padrona di casa.
answer.en: It's the bank my landlady recommended.

ask.said: Com'è il tuo conto nuovo?
ask.en: How's your new account?

answer.said: Il conto che ho aperto è gratuito.
answer.en: The account I opened is free.

ask.said: Quale carta ti ha mangiato il bancomat?
ask.en: Which card did the ATM eat?

answer.said: Quella che mi ha dato la banca la settimana scorsa.
answer.en: The one the bank gave me last week.

mission.goal: Tell the clerk who recommended this bank.

say.said: È la banca che mi ha consigliato la padrona di casa.
say.en: It's the bank my landlady recommended.

steps.title: The person you spoke to
steps.how_to: How to say "the person I spoke to" with con cui, di cui and per cui.
steps.intro: After a word like con, di or per, Italian uses cui, as in la persona con cui ho parlato. You'll use it to explain who and what you mean at the bank.

examples.said: La persona con cui ho parlato ieri oggi non c'è.
examples.en: The person I talked to yesterday isn't here today.

examples.said: È questo il documento di cui ho bisogno?
examples.en: Is this the document I need?

examples.said: È un servizio con cui la banca paga le bollette ogni mese.
examples.en: It's a service the bank uses to pay your bills every month.

examples.said: Il titolare è la persona alla quale è intestata la carta.
examples.en: The account holder is the person whose name is on the card.

steps.notice: The little word comes first and cui follows, because an Italian sentence never ends on con or di; contracts write alla quale where people say a cui.

ask.said: Chi cerchi in banca?
ask.en: Who are you looking for at the bank?

answer.said: Cerco la persona con cui ho parlato ieri.
answer.en: I'm looking for the person I talked to yesterday.

ask.said: Perché sei in banca oggi?
ask.en: Why are you at the bank today?

answer.said: Il motivo per cui sono qui è aprire un conto.
answer.en: The reason I'm here is to open an account.

ask.said: Per aprire il conto, cosa chiedi all'impiegato?
ask.en: To open the account, what do you ask the clerk?

answer.said: Qual è il documento di cui ho bisogno?
answer.en: Which document do I need?

mission.goal: Ask for the clerk you talked to yesterday.

say.said: Cerco la persona con cui ho parlato ieri.
say.en: I'm looking for the person I talked to yesterday.

steps.title: Where and when it happened
steps.how_to: How to say "the branch where" and "the day when" with dove and in cui.
steps.intro: Dove and in cui describe a place, and in cui also describes a time. You'll use them to say where your account is and when something happened.

examples.said: È la filiale dove ho il conto.
examples.en: It's the branch where I have my account.

examples.said: Questa è la filiale in cui ho aperto il conto.
examples.en: This is the branch where I opened my account.

examples.said: Il giorno in cui ho firmato il contratto, mi hanno dato il bancomat.
examples.en: The day I signed the contract, they gave me my debit card.

steps.notice: For a place you can say dove or in cui, but for a time only in cui, because dove is just for places.

ask.said: Dove vai per prelevare?
ask.en: Where do you go to take out cash?

answer.said: Vado alla filiale dove ho il conto.
answer.en: I go to the branch where I have my account.

ask.said: Quando hai ricevuto il bancomat?
ask.en: When did you get your debit card?

answer.said: Il giorno in cui ho aperto il conto.
answer.en: The day I opened my account.

ask.said: In quale filiale ritiri la carta?
ask.en: Which branch do you pick up your card at?

answer.said: In quella dove ho aperto il conto.
answer.en: At the one where I opened my account.

mission.goal: Check that you're at the branch that has your account.

say.said: È questa la filiale dove ho il conto?
say.en: Is this the branch where my account is?

steps.title: What you don't understand
steps.how_to: How to say "what" meaning "the thing that" with quello che.
steps.intro: Quello che means "what" in the sense of "the thing that." You'll use it to say what you don't understand and what you were looking for.

examples.said: Non capisco bene quello che c'è scritto qui.
examples.en: I don't really understand what it says here.

examples.said: Mi scusi, non capisco quello che dice.
examples.en: Excuse me, I don't understand what you're saying.

examples.said: È proprio quello che cercavo.
examples.en: It's just what I was looking for.

examples.said: Ciò che conta è la firma.
examples.en: What matters is the signature.

steps.notice: When "what" means "the thing that," Italian says quello che, or ciò che when it's more formal, because che alone can't stand for the thing.

ask.said: Il contratto è difficile. Cosa dici all'impiegato?
ask.en: The contract is hard to follow. What do you tell the clerk?

answer.said: Non capisco bene quello che c'è scritto qui.
answer.en: I don't really understand what it says here.

ask.said: Trovi il regalo perfetto per un'amica. Cosa dici?
ask.en: You find the perfect gift for a friend. What do you say?

answer.said: È proprio quello che cercavo!
answer.en: It's just what I was looking for!

ask.said: In un conto corrente, cosa conta di più per te?
ask.en: In a checking account, what matters most to you?

answer.said: Quello che conta è il canone mensile.
answer.en: What matters is the monthly fee.

mission.goal: Tell the clerk which part of the contract you don't understand.

say.said: Non capisco bene quello che c'è scritto qui.
say.en: I don't really understand what it says here.

steps.title: Before you sign
steps.how_to: How to say "before doing something" with prima di.
steps.intro: Prima di plus a verb means "before doing something." You'll use it at the bank to read the terms before you sign.

examples.said: Prima di firmare, vorrei leggere le condizioni.
examples.en: Before I sign, I'd like to read the terms.

examples.said: Prima di aprire il conto, mi serve il Suo codice fiscale.
examples.en: Before we open the account, I need your tax code.

examples.said: Prima di firmare, leggo sempre il contratto.
examples.en: I always read the contract before I sign.

steps.notice: "Before doing" is prima di plus the -re form of the verb, because Italian has no -ing form here.
steps.context: Many Italian checking accounts charge a monthly fee, so people ask about the spese mensili before opening one.

ask.said: L'impiegato ti dà il contratto. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: The clerk hands you the contract. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Prima di firmare, vorrei leggere le condizioni.
answer.en: Before I sign, I'd like to read the terms.

ask.said: Cosa ti serve per aprire un conto?
ask.en: What do you need to open an account?

answer.said: Prima di aprire il conto, mi serve il codice fiscale.
answer.en: Before I open the account, I need my tax code.

ask.said: Cosa chiedi in banca prima di tutto?
ask.en: What do you ask at the bank first of all?

answer.said: Prima di aprire il conto, vorrei sapere le spese mensili.
answer.en: Before I open the account, I'd like to know the monthly fees.

mission.goal: Ask to read the terms before you sign.

say.said: Prima di firmare, vorrei leggere le condizioni.
say.en: Before I sign, I'd like to read the terms.

steps.title: Comparing two apartments
steps.how_to: How to say "than" with di or che when you compare.
steps.intro: To compare two things, Italian says "than" with di or with che. You'll use it to weigh up two apartments.

examples.said: Questo è più luminoso dell'altro.
examples.en: This one's brighter than the other one.

examples.said: Sì, ma è più piccolo di questo.
examples.en: Yes, but it's smaller than this one.

examples.said: La strada è più rumorosa di giorno che di notte.
examples.en: The street is noisier during the day than at night.

examples.said: È più bello che comodo.
examples.en: It's more beautiful than comfortable.

steps.notice: Before a thing or a word like questo, "than" is di; before an adjective or a phrase like di notte it's che, because you're comparing two qualities or two times of the same thing.

ask.said: Hai visto due appartamenti. Com'è il primo rispetto al secondo?
ask.en: You saw two apartments. How does the first compare to the second?

answer.said: Il primo è più grande del secondo.
answer.en: The first one is bigger than the second.

ask.said: Il monolocale ti piace?
ask.en: Do you like the studio?

answer.said: Sì, ma è più bello che comodo.
answer.en: Yes, but it's more beautiful than comfortable.

ask.said: Com'è la tua strada, di giorno e di notte?
ask.en: What's your street like, during the day and at night?

answer.said: È più rumorosa di giorno che di notte.
answer.en: It's noisier during the day than at night.

mission.goal: Compare two apartments with a friend.

say.said: Questo è più luminoso dell'altro.
say.en: This one's brighter than the other one.

steps.title: The best and the worst
steps.how_to: How to say "the most," "the best" and "very" about a place.
steps.intro: Il più says "the most," il migliore says "the best," and -issimo says "very." You'll use them to pick an apartment and talk about the neighborhood.

examples.said: È il più grande che abbiamo visto.
examples.en: It's the biggest one we've seen.

examples.said: Allora secondo me è il migliore.
examples.en: Then I think it's the best one.

examples.said: È il bilocale più luminoso del palazzo.
examples.en: It's the brightest one-bedroom in the building.

examples.said: La zona è tranquillissima.
examples.en: The neighborhood is really quiet.

steps.notice: "The most" is il più plus the adjective, with di for the group, as in del palazzo; il migliore already means "the best," and -issimo means "very."

ask.said: Com'è la tua zona?
ask.en: What's your neighborhood like?

answer.said: È tranquillissima.
answer.en: It's really quiet.

ask.said: Hai visto tre bilocali. Quale prendi?
ask.en: You saw three one-bedrooms. Which one are you taking?

answer.said: Prendo questo: è il più luminoso dei tre.
answer.en: I'm taking this one. It's the brightest of the three.

ask.said: E l'appartamento vicino al mercato, com'era?
ask.en: And the apartment near the market, what was it like?

answer.said: Era pessimo.
answer.en: It was terrible.

mission.goal: Tell a friend which apartment is the best.

say.said: Secondo me questo è il migliore.
say.en: I think this one's the best.

steps.title: How long it's been
steps.how_to: How to say how long something has been going on with sono... che.
steps.intro: Sono due settimane che plus the present says how long something has been going on. You'll use it to chase a repair with your landlady.

examples.said: Sono già due settimane che aspetto l'idraulico.
examples.en: I've been waiting for the plumber for two weeks already.

examples.said: È un mese che il citofono non funziona.
examples.en: The buzzer hasn't worked in a month.

examples.said: Abito qui da sei mesi.
examples.en: I've lived here for six months.

steps.notice: For something that started in the past and is still going on, Italian uses the present, because it isn't over: sono due settimane che aspetto, or aspetto da due settimane; with one week or month, it's è.

ask.said: Da quanto tempo abiti qui?
ask.en: How long have you lived here?

answer.said: Abito qui da … mesi.
answer.en: I've lived here for … months.

ask.said: La caldaia è ancora rotta. Cosa dici alla padrona di casa?
ask.en: The boiler's still broken. What do you tell your landlady?

answer.said: Sono già due settimane che aspetto l'idraulico.
answer.en: I've been waiting for the plumber for two weeks already.

ask.said: Il citofono è ancora rotto. Cosa dici all'amministratore?
ask.en: The buzzer's still broken. What do you tell the building manager?

answer.said: È un mese che il citofono non funziona.
answer.en: The buzzer hasn't worked in a month.

mission.goal: Tell your landlady how long you've been waiting for the plumber.

say.said: Sono già due settimane che aspetto l'idraulico.
say.en: I've been waiting for the plumber for two weeks already.

steps.title: Describing the one you want
steps.how_to: How to describe an apartment or a person with che and in cui.
steps.intro: Che and in cui let you say which apartment, area or person you mean. You'll use them when you choose a place and deal with repairs.

examples.said: Allora, prendi il bilocale che abbiamo visto ieri?
examples.en: So, are you taking the one-bedroom we saw yesterday?

examples.said: La zona in cui vorrei vivere è vicino al mercato.
examples.en: The area I'd like to live in is near the market.

examples.said: L'idraulico che chiamo di solito è in ferie.
examples.en: The plumber I usually call is on vacation.

steps.notice: To say which one you mean, add che plus what you say about it, or a little word like in plus cui, as in la zona in cui vorrei vivere.

ask.said: Quale appartamento ti piace di più?
ask.en: Which apartment do you like best?

answer.said: Mi piace il bilocale che abbiamo visto ieri.
answer.en: I like the one-bedroom we saw yesterday.

ask.said: In quale zona vorresti vivere?
ask.en: What area would you like to live in?

answer.said: La zona in cui vorrei vivere è vicino a …
answer.en: The area I'd like to live in is near …

ask.said: Chi chiami se la caldaia è rotta?
ask.en: Who do you call if the boiler breaks?

answer.said: Chiamo l'idraulico che mi ha consigliato la padrona di casa.
answer.en: I call the plumber my landlady recommended.

mission.goal: Tell a friend which apartment you prefer.

say.said: Preferisco il bilocale che abbiamo visto ieri.
say.en: I prefer the one-bedroom we saw yesterday.
